newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian stocks limp lower, seen shackled.
newsitem.headline: Austrian stocks limp lower, seen shackled.

text.p: Austrian shares kick off the week on a limp note, with active participation discouraged by a lower dollar and weak German leads, traders said.
Opinions are split over the market's short-term direction after the ATX index lost 11.60 points or 0.89 percent to end at 1,290.87 with 18 shares falling, and just three gaining.

One trader said that the ATX index would "run out of steam" at 1,300 points and would "tend towards the downside". But another said the ATX was currently consolidating a bottom and was poised for a resurgence of investor demand.

The consolidation would continue at the most down to 1,280 points. "That would be the lowest point we could reach in the next few days," he said, adding that today's losses were largely due to a lack of trading volume.
Wolford, the manufacturer of luxury hosiery and lingerie, led decliners, shedding 4.53 percent to close at a new low for the year of 1,116.95 schillings.
The day's top performing stock was Creditanstalt ordinaries, up 0.27 percent at 706 schillings.
The broad-based Vienna bourse index lost 2.88 points, or 0.61 percent, to 473.11.
The July ATX futures contract fell 18 points to 1,290 on turnover of 407 lots. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 256
